observations: Photos 0, 1 and 2 show the same used automatic gearbox lying on bare ground in a parts yard.
A transfer case is bolted to the rear of the gearbox, so it is a 4WD unit.
Bell housing with a yellow paint dot at the front; no torque converter is visible in it.
Wiring harness with plug connectors, metal cooler lines and a long dipstick tube are still attached.
Casing is dusty and oily; no ID tag, part number or casting text can be read in any photo.
A second gearbox lies to the left under a tarpaulin; watermark reads 'POSTED ON JIJI' and 'GEARUP INC'.

identity.kind: used automatic gearbox with 4WD transfer case (vehicle fitment unread)

claims.evidence: No ID tag or part number is readable in photos 0-2; the shape alone does not prove the fitment.
Engine size cannot be read from the casing in any photo.
Photos 0-2 show a transfer case bolted to the gearbox.
Origin cannot be shown by photos.

risks.risk: Gearbox is not the Ford Expedition V8 unit claimed, so it does not fit the buyer's market.
risks.proof: Close, sharp photo of the gearbox ID tag or cast part number on the casing.
risks.if_unproven: Cannot be priced for a specific vehicle; held until the tag is read.

risks.risk: Internal wear: slipping, harsh shifts or no drive.
risks.proof: Video of it running in a vehicle before removal, or a test on a bench by the agent.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as not working, a core unit for rebuild.

risks.proof: Photo straight into the bell housing.

risks.risk: Transfer case damaged or its shift motor faulty.
risks.proof: Close photo of the transfer case, its motor and output flanges, plus a clip turning the output shaft.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as a gearbox with a faulty transfer case.

risks.risk: Cracked casing or burnt fluid inside.
risks.proof: Photo of the fluid on the dipstick and close shots of the casing underside.

proof_requests: Close photo of the gearbox ID tag or cast part number.
Photo looking into the bell housing to show the torque converter.
Photo of the fluid on the dipstick.
Close photos of the transfer case and its shift motor.
Clip of the unit running in a vehicle before removal, if any.
response.reason: It is clearly a used automatic gearbox with a 4WD transfer case, but its fitment, which sets the price, is not readable on any photo and rests only on the seller's words. A shot of the ID tag is needed before a worst case price can be set.
